To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cooperative structures of QDs–pits on InAs substrate were obtained for the first time; the cooperative QDs–piths structures were obtained for the InAs1–xSbxP1–y quantum dots on InAs(1 0 0) substrate by liquid phase epitaxial growth; the QDs and pits are formed by the same bimodal growth mechanism; the QDs–pitts cooperative structures are obtained due to Sb and P segregation in
the InAsSb1–xPx QDs and pits are formed on the InAs(100)-oriented substrates by LPE.
the InAsSb0.2P0.2P QDs–pits cooperative growth on InAs substrate by liquid phase epitaxial technique is reported.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of the InAsSb1−xP x QDs, pits, and dots–pots cooperative structures on InAs(001) substrates, and the interaction of the dots and pits during their cooperative growth.
the growth of QDs and pits, as well their cooperative structures on the InAs(100)-based substrate.
the formation of the cooperative structures consisting of the QDs and pits on InAs substrate.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the QDs and the pits are nucleated and developed in the cooperative manner, and the QDs are banded by the pits.
the InAsSb/P QDs–pits structures can be grown on InAs(001) substrates.
the InAsSb/P quantum dots and pits cooperative nucleation on InAs(001) substrate is caused by the surface segregation of Sb and P atoms, which are the most mobile atoms in InAsSb(P) alloys.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QDs and pits cooperative structures can be used in the design of the new generation of the optoelectronic devices.
the cooperative growth of the QDs and pits is possible by the liquid phase epitaxy technique and the QDs–pits cooperative structure can be used for the long wavelength infrared detectors.
the cooperative nucleation of the QDs–pits structures is a new approach for the fabrication of novel semiconductor materials and devices with unique optical properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the InAsSb/P QDs and pits cooperative structures can be used for fabrication of the photovoltaic and optoelectronic devices operating at 1.55–3.0 μm.
the InAsSb0.2P0.2/InAs(100) system can be a good candidate for the fabrication of quantum dots and pits arrays with controllable dimensions and density.
the cooperative nucleation of the QDs and pits on InAs(1 0 0) substrate is possible by the LPE method.
